name: Tesamorelin
used_for: FDA-labeled for reduction of excess abdominal fat in HIV-infected adults with lipodystrophy; not indicated for general weight loss.

entries.text: Egrifta SV: labeled dose 1.4 mg (0.35 mL of reconstituted solution) injected subcutaneously once daily in the abdomen.
entries.population: HIV-infected adults with lipodystrophy and excess abdominal fat

entries.text: Egrifta WR: labeled dose 1.28 mg (0.16 mL of reconstituted solution) injected subcutaneously once daily in the abdomen; one vial is reconstituted to provide seven daily doses.
entries.population: HIV-infected adults with lipodystrophy and excess abdominal fat

internet_entries.text: An independent peptide information website (Peptide Library) says community users describe 2 mg subcutaneously daily (matching the approved dose), 1 mg daily as a cost-conscious level, and 1 mg at night combined with 100 mcg ipamorelin morning and evening. These are described as off-label community practices.
internet_entries.population: As described by the source, not a study population

administration_guidance.text: Egrifta SV label: unreconstituted vials are stored at room temperature in the original box, protected from light.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: Egrifta SV label: the solution is administered immediately after reconstitution; it is not stored, frozen or refrigerated, and unused solution is discarded.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: Egrifta WR label: one reconstituted vial provides doses for 7 consecutive days, kept at room temperature (not frozen), and any remaining solution is discarded after 7 days.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: Egrifta WR label: the bacteriostatic water diluent is discarded 28 days after first use.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: Labels state the injection goes subcutaneously into the abdomen with rotating sites, avoiding the navel, scar tissue and bruises.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: Egrifta SV label: the powder is reconstituted with the supplied diluent and mixed by rolling the vial gently in the hands for 30 seconds, without shaking.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: Egrifta SV label: sites are chosen at least 2 inches (5 cm) from the navel. The label's administration section names no required time of day and no food restriction.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: The Peptidepedia website says tesamorelin is injected either in the morning on an empty stomach (at least 2 hours after eating and 30 to 60 minutes before food) or at bedtime, and that a vial mixed with bacteriostatic water is refrigerated, protected from light, not frozen and used within 14 to 28 days. This differs from the approved label, which names no time of day and says a reconstituted vial is used immediately or, for the weekly-vial product, kept at room temperature for 7 days.
administration_guidance.label: internet

administration_guidance.text: A compounded-peptide telehealth seller (FormBlends) says tesamorelin is injected once daily at bedtime on an empty stomach, with no food for at least 2 hours beforehand, and that a reconstituted vial is refrigerated and used within 24 hours. The company sells compounded tesamorelin.
administration_guidance.label: internet

side_effects.text: Egrifta SV label: injection site reactions 17% vs 6% placebo, arthralgia 13% vs 11%, peripheral edema 6% vs 2%, and myalgia 6% vs 2%.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: Label warnings: increased risk of neoplasms (preexisting malignancy should be inactive), elevated IGF-1, fluid retention (edema, arthralgia, carpal tunnel syndrome), glucose intolerance (elevated HbA1c in 5% vs 1% placebo), hypersensitivity reactions (4%), and increased mortality in critically ill patients.
side_effects.label: research

internet_claims.claim: Patient reviews of Egrifta WR are mixed: some describe reduced belly fat and easier movement, while others report no benefit, joint pain, hand numbness, preparation difficulty, and cost or supply problems.
Project Biohacking says tesamorelin mainly cuts deep belly fat (roughly 15 to 18 percent) and may preserve or modestly add lean mass, but warns that calling it a muscle builder oversells it.

Swolverine, a supplement brand's bodybuilding blog, argues tesamorelin raises natural growth hormone and IGF-1, targets stubborn abdominal fat while keeping lean tissue during a cut, and speeds recovery.

A longevity clinic's blog (the Evergreen Institute, which also promotes consultations) presents tesamorelin as a well-studied peptide that lowers visceral and liver fat and preserves muscle, and that clinicians may consider it beyond its HIV indication.

research.summary: FDA-approved DailyMed prescribing information for Egrifta SV (tesamorelin) for injection.
research.finding: Indicated to reduce excess abdominal fat in HIV-infected adults with lipodystrophy; not for general weight management.

research.summary: FDA-approved DailyMed prescribing information for Egrifta WR (tesamorelin) for injection.
research.finding: Same indication as Egrifta SV with a weekly-reconstitution format; long-term cardiovascular safety has not been established.

research.summary: Randomized placebo-controlled trial with safety extension of tesamorelin in HIV-infected patients with abdominal fat accumulation (Falutz et al., J Acquir Immune Defic Syndr).
research.finding: Visceral fat fell about 10.9% with tesamorelin versus 0.6% with placebo over 6 months; gains were lost after switching to placebo.

research.summary: Pooled analysis of two phase 3 trials (806 patients) of tesamorelin 2 mg daily versus placebo for 26 weeks, with a 26-week extension (Falutz et al., J Clin Endocrinol Metab).
research.finding: Visceral fat decreased significantly versus placebo (treatment effect -15.4%) with lower triglycerides and no meaningful change in subcutaneous abdominal fat.

research.summary: 12-week randomized placebo-controlled dose-ranging trial of tesamorelin 1 mg or 2 mg daily in 61 HIV-infected patients with abdominal fat accumulation (Falutz et al., AIDS).
research.finding: IGF-1 rose 48% on 1 mg and 65% on 2 mg versus placebo; trunk fat fell 9.2% on 2 mg, a significant drop versus placebo, while 1 mg did not reach significance.

research.summary: Study in 7 healthy young adults of how an oral glucose load and arginine change the growth hormone response to injected GHRH (Ghigo et al., Metabolism).
research.finding: Oral glucose beforehand lowered the GH peak after GHRH from 11.6 to 7.4 micrograms per liter; the authors suggest, from indirect evidence, that glucose acts by raising hypothalamic somatostatin.

research.summary: Frequent-sampling study of 24-hour growth hormone secretion in 6 healthy men on a fed day and on days 1 and 5 of a 5-day fast (Ho et al., J Clin Invest).
research.finding: Fasting increased growth hormone secretion and amplified its daily rhythms compared with the fed day.

research.summary: Study of growth hormone secretion in healthy men in relation to sleep and time of day, using deconvolution of frequent blood samples (Van Cauter et al., J Clin Endocrinol Metab).
research.finding: A GH pulse began within 30 minutes of sleep onset in every profile with normal sleep, and about 70% of pulses during sleep were tied to slow-wave sleep.

research.summary: Review of the relationship between growth hormone secretion and sleep (Van Cauter et al., Growth Horm IGF Res).
research.finding: In men a sleep-onset pulse is usually the main daily episode of GH secretion, and GH secretion tracks the amount of slow-wave sleep.

dose.summary: 1.4 mg daily (Egrifta SV) or 1.28 mg daily (Egrifta WR) per the FDA labels. Online sources describe 1 to 2 mg daily. No dose above 2 mg has been tested.

items.text: FDA label: 1.4 mg once daily for Egrifta SV, injected under the skin of the abdomen. Labeled for HIV-infected adults with lipodystrophy.
items.label: research

items.text: FDA label: 1.28 mg once daily for Egrifta WR. The label says this gives similar exposure to the 2 mg daily dose of the original formulation used in the pivotal trials.
items.label: research

items.text: A 12-week dose-ranging trial compared 1 mg and 2 mg daily. Only 2 mg cut trunk fat significantly versus placebo, and it raised IGF-1 more. No higher dose has been tested in a published trial.
items.label: research

items.text: Peptide Library says community users describe 2 mg daily, 1 mg daily as a cheaper option, and 1 mg at night combined with ipamorelin. These are off-label practices.
items.label: internet

items.text: Perfect B, a clinic that sells tesamorelin, describes 1 mg per injection in month 1 and 1.5 mg in months 2 and 3, mixed with ipamorelin.
items.label: internet

timing.summary: The labels name no time of day. Online sources favor bedtime, to match the natural overnight GH pulse; bedtime dosing has not been tested.

items.text: The labels name no time of day.
items.label: research

items.text: The body's own largest GH pulse comes shortly after falling asleep, during deep sleep. This is natural GH, not tesamorelin; no trial has compared bedtime with daytime dosing.
items.label: research

items.text: Peptidepedia says tesamorelin is taken either in the morning on an empty stomach or at bedtime.
items.label: internet

items.text: FormBlends, a compounded-peptide seller, says once daily at bedtime.
items.label: internet

fasting.summary: The labels set no food rule. Online sources say 2 hours without food first, based on studies where glucose blunted the GH response to natural GHRH.

items.text: The labels set no food restriction.
items.label: research

items.text: In healthy adults, a glucose drink before an injection of natural GHRH lowered the GH response by about a third; the authors suggest somatostatin as the reason. Tesamorelin works like GHRH, but no study has tested meals with tesamorelin.
items.label: research

items.text: In healthy men, fasting increased the body's own GH secretion compared with a fed day.
items.label: research

items.text: Peptidepedia says morning doses go at least 2 hours after eating and 30 to 60 minutes before food.
items.label: internet

items.text: FormBlends says no food for at least 2 hours before a bedtime dose.
items.label: internet

frequency.summary: Once daily, every day, per the labels and trials. Online sources describe 5 days on, 2 off, which differs from the label.

items.text: Once daily, every day, in the labels and in every pivotal trial.
items.label: research

items.text: Peptidepedia says some practitioners use 5 days on and 2 days off, and that trial data for cycling are limited because the pivotal trials used continuous daily dosing.
items.label: internet

items.text: HealthRx says a small number of clinicians use 2 mg on a 5 days on, 2 days off schedule, and found no trial testing it.
items.label: internet

items.text: Perfect B describes 5 days on and 2 days off as its standard schedule.
items.label: internet

cycle_length.summary: Trials ran daily for 26 to 52 weeks with no break, and visceral fat returned after stopping. Online sources describe 8 to 12 weeks on, then a break.

items.text: The pivotal trials gave daily treatment for 26 weeks, then continued to 52 weeks. Patients switched to placebo regained visceral fat (up 22% and 16%), while those who stayed on tesamorelin kept the reduction. No break was studied.
items.label: research

items.text: Peptidepedia says some practitioners use 8 to 12 weeks on, then 4 weeks off, and that clinical evidence for any cycling protocol is lacking.
items.label: internet

items.text: Perfect B describes 3 months on, then a 2-month break.
items.label: internet

storage_and_handling.summary: Powder is kept at room temperature. Egrifta SV is used right after mixing; an Egrifta WR vial lasts 7 days. Online sources say to refrigerate, which differs from the label.

mechanism.summary: Makes the pituitary release the body's own growth hormone (GH) in pulses, which raises IGF-1.

items.text: A lab-made version of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH). It acts on the pituitary to make and release the body's own GH in pulses, which raises IGF-1. Some GH effects run through IGF-1 made in the liver and other tissues.
items.label: research

items.text: In a 12-week trial IGF-1 rose 48% on 1 mg and 65% on 2 mg versus placebo.
items.label: research

best_documented_effect.summary: Visceral fat fell 14 to 18% at 26 weeks in HIV-infected adults with lipodystrophy, with no weight change.

items.text: Visceral (deep belly) fat reduction: down 18% and 14% at 26 weeks on 2 mg daily, versus up 2% and down 2% on placebo, in HIV-infected adults with lipodystrophy. Body weight did not change, and the label says it is not for weight loss.
items.label: research
